title: How Pavel Durov grew Telegram to ~900M users with zero ad spend, 30 engineers and no outside equity
summary: Durov explains how Telegram grew organically to nearly 900M users on product quality alone, run by a tiny elite engineering team with him as sole owner and product manager. He also covers refusing government pressure, picking a neutral base (Dubai), and avoiding investors and material assets to stay free.

principles.text: Spend nothing on user acquisition; grow organically because people prefer better products and recommend them.
principles.quote: we've never spent anything on acquiring users for marketing purposes we never promoted telegram uh you know on other social Platforms in any way

principles.text: Quality drives word of mouth: users who discover the speed, security and features won't go back and invite friends.
principles.quote: people are smart people like to use good things and they don't like to use inferior things

principles.text: Keep a tiny, elite engineering team and find talent through public contests instead of an HR department.
principles.quote: we select the best of the best Engineers as a result of the competitions that we organize

principles.text: Stay sole owner and product manager to move faster; avoid outside equity so investors' goals don't conflict with the mission.
principles.quote: having my myself as the sole owner director and product manager for this uh extensive period of time and the company's development allowed us to move faster

principles.text: Private companies are more efficient than public ones; public listing adds bureaucracy and pressure to keep headcount high.
principles.quote: running a public company is uh less efficient than running a private company because you have to be accountable to much more people

principles.text: Stay focused on the product: avoid assets and distractions that tie you down or consume attention.
principles.quote: I would rather make decisions that would influence how a billion people communicate rather than choosing the color of seats in the house
